My land is about 10 mu here in Quzhou. I have been farming this same land since I was young, watching my parents do it, and their parents before them. I do not read, but I know this soil.

The only real question is how much wheat and how much maize — and the answer is the same as last year, and the year before. Everyone here does wheat and maize. The land tells you what it wants. In winter I put in wheat, in summer I rotate to maize. That is how we do it.

I will plant 8 mu of wheat starting in October. I buy the improved seed from the village supply store — the man there tells me which one, and I trust him because my neighbor used the same one and got a good harvest. For fertilizer I apply the compound bag at planting, then urea again in spring when the stalks start shooting up. For water I pump three times — once before sowing to wet the ground, once in spring, once when the heads come out. I spray twice: once in winter for the weeds, once before summer for the bugs and rust.

After the wheat comes off in June, I plant maize on the same 8 mu right away without tilling — the soil is already loose and I do not want to waste time or diesel. The hybrid seed is more expensive but the yield is worth it. My son helped me buy the right bags last year and I will do the same again. Maize needs less water in summer because the rains come, but I still pump twice to be safe.

I keep 2 mu near the house for vegetables — eggplant, beans, garlic — mostly to eat, maybe sell a little at the village market.
